note: [L] never states `η₂ = (2·1_[1/2,1]) *_M (2·1_[1/2,1])` as a function identity (`eta2` is defined directly by `4 max(log 2 - |log 2t|, 0)`, Helfgott/Defs.lean:44-46); it proves the same convolution integral only at points `t = mn/x` with integers `m, n`, with the substitution `w = n/W` and mixed strict/non-strict inequalities.

snippet.text:
theorem eta2_eq_integral {x : ℝ} (hx : 0 < x) {m n : ℕ} (hm : 1 ≤ m) (hn : 1 ≤ n) {A B : ℝ}
    (hA : 0 < A) (hAB : A ≤ B) (hAlo : A ≤ max (x / (2 * m)) n)
    (hhiB : min (x / m) (2 * n) ≤ B) :
    eta2 (m * n / x) = 4 * ∫ W in A..B,
      (if x / (2 * W) < m ∧ (m : ℝ) ≤ x / W ∧ W / 2 < n ∧ (n : ℝ) ≤ W then 1 / W else 0) := by
  have hm0 : (0 : ℝ) < m := by exact_mod_cast hm

proof_context.conclusion: For positive integers `m, n`: `η₂(mn/x) = 4∫ 1[x/2W < m ≤ x/W, W/2 < n ≤ W] dW/W`, the Mellin convolution of `2·1_[1/2,1]` with itself written as an integral over `W` of two interval indicators.
